title: Rabbi Abba bar Avina

paragraphs:
(In the Yerushalmi: R' Ba bar Buna, or Bina, and sometimes Mina, since bet and mem interchange.) In Hyman’s reconstruction, apparently he was a Jerusalemite [or: from Eretz Israel] and learned Torah from Rav while still in Eretz Israel. This is what we find in Bava Metzia ch. 4 halakhah 1 and Sanhedrin ch. 3 halakhah 3, where he speaks in Rav's name. And in Bava Metzia ch. 1, end of halakhah 4, he had fields which he gave out on sharecropping; and once [supplied ופ״א ופעם אחת] his sharecropper climbed a date palm, found fledglings, and took them [ונסתון]. In Hyman’s telling, he went and asked Rav, who said nothing to him; he went and returned the fledglings to their place. R' Ba bar Mina said: Why did you hurry to return them, before we told you a clear ruling? He was also a judge in his town, as in Bava Metzia ch. 5 halakhah 1: a certain man borrowed dinars from his fellow - the case came before R' Ba bar Mina, etc.
Hyman writes that he merited to raise students who were great men of the generation, as we find in Shabbat 60b that R' Abba bar Zavda asked him: if one shaped it [the nail] like a clamp [כלבוס], what is the law? He said to him: permitted. We likewise find R' Berekhiah citing him in Yoma, end of ch. 8; and R' Patroki, brother of R' Drusa, citing him in Yoma ch. 4 halakhah 4.

We find that he had a brother named Hagra, in Megillah ch. 1 halakhah 9, 12a. His statements are found: Shabbat ch. 2 halakhah 6, that Satan accuses only at a time of danger; Yoma ch. 1, beginning of halakhah 1, he said: why did Scripture juxtapose the passage of Miriam to the passage of the red heifer? This statement is also cited in his name in Vayikra Rabbah, end of ch. 20, and in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 174, in Hyman’s judgment, mistakenly in the name of Abba bar Zavina, and Hyman says it should read Bina.

And in Ketubot ch. 1, beginning of halakhah 2, Chuna in the name of Shmuel, regarding the holy shekel: R' Ba bar Bina said: it is current coinage. He is likewise mentioned in Devarim Rabbah, beginning of ch. 9: from where [do we learn] seven days of mourning? He said: for so we find with Yosef, etc.

The named Shabbat60b paragraph concerns shaping a sandal nail like tongs, so [the nail] identifies the referent omitted from Hyman’s compressed question. The earlier perfume/scented-garment proposal is not restored. The named Yerushalmi BavaMetzia1:4 paragraph says the sharecropper took the chicks and asked לרב, rendered the master by Guggenheimer; this does not independently establish Hyman’s identification with Rav or settle every pronoun in his expanded narrative.

In ופ״א ופעם אחת, the explicit ופעם אחת supplies the sense once for the adjoining abbreviation; this is not a second chapter-one citation. The redundant supplied wording remains displayed without a source edit.

The actual named digital parallels preserve different forms: Bava Metzia 4:1 has Rabbi Abba bar Mina in Rav’s name, while Sanhedrin 3:3 has Rava bar Bina in Rav’s name. The sharecropper passage’s לרב is translated “the master” by Guggenheimer; his commentary also reports a possible Abba bar Zamina identification, which is not adopted here. Hyman’s Rav identification, expanded returning dialogue, geographical and teacher reconstruction, and proposed letter interchange remain his claims. Megillah 1:9 expressly calls Hagra the brother of Rabbi Ba bar Bina; Yoma 8:7 has Berekhiah citing Rabbi Ba bar Bina, and 4:4 has Patroki, brother of Derosa, citing him. Shabbat 2:6 and Yoma 1:1 also name Rabbi Ba bar Bina, while Vayikra Rabbah 20:12 names Rabbi Abba bar Avina. Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 26:11 has the abbreviated R’ Abba bar Zevina beside Hyman’s supplied old folio 174 and his insistence that Bina should be read; this comparison does not prove a printed correction history. Ketubot 1:2 and Devarim Rabbah 9:1 support the separate coinage and mourning notices. The source’s actor and identification questions remain held.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, pp. 14–15) uses a single ופ״א (“once”) and prints כמין כלבוס (“like tongs”). The supplied Hebrew repeats “once” and has שמין. Shabbat 60b gives the question about a sandal nail shaped like tongs. In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 1:4, the sharecropper takes the chicks, consults the master in Guggenheimer’s translation, and returns them. Rabbi Ba bar Mina says the returning is more difficult than the finding. Hyman identifies the master as Rav and retells the last remark as a question about returning too hastily.

The consulted Bava Metzia 4:1 names Abba bar Mina, and Sanhedrin 3:3 names Rava bar Bina, both in Rav’s name. The other consulted passages preserve their local forms. Megillah 1:9 names Hagra as the brother of Ba bar Bina, and Vayikra Rabbah 20:12 names Abba bar Avina in the Miriam teaching where Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 26:11 has Abba bar Zevina. Hyman’s reading Bina in the Pesikta and his account of the teacher relationship and place of origin are his reconstruction.
